title: Karn Sharma, 38, Retires From All Cricket After Record-Setting IPL Career Across Four Franchises
excerpt: The leg-spinner who won three consecutive IPL titles with three different teams announced his retirement during the UP T20 League in Lucknow.
body:
• Karn Sharma, 38, announced his retirement from all forms of cricket on August 23, 2026, during the UP T20 League match between Kanpur Superstars and Meerut Mavericks.
  • The leg-spinner holds the unique record of winning three consecutive IPL titles with three different franchises — Sunrisers Hyderabad (2016), Mumbai Indians (2017) and Chennai Super Kings (2018).
  • Sharma played one Test, two ODIs and one T20I for India, all in 2014, becoming the first Indian leg-spinner to debut in Australia in 25 years.
  • He represented Railways for most of his domestic career, taking 257 wickets in 91 first-class matches at an average of 27.15.

A Quiet Exit After a Journeyman Career

Karn Sharma announced his retirement from all forms of cricket on Saturday night in Lucknow, bringing down the curtain on a career that spanned nearly two decades and produced one of the most unusual records in Indian Premier League history.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=aOsbos6gj9I

The 38-year-old leg-spinner made the announcement after a UP T20 League match between his team, the Kanpur Superstars, and the Kashi Rudras. He will play his final match on August 25 during the Lucknow leg of the tournament before formally stepping away.

"I want to retire now," Sharma said. "I am very grateful to my family, BCCI, Railways, UPCA, Andhra, Vidarbha Cricket Association and all the people who supported me through this journey."

Three Titles, Three Teams, Three Years

Sharma's career will be remembered above all for an IPL achievement that remains unmatched. Between 2016 and 2018, he won three consecutive IPL titles with three different franchises: Sunrisers Hyderabad in 2016, Mumbai Indians in 2017 and Chennai Super Kings in 2018.

The record speaks to both his value as a squad player and the nature of the IPL's franchise system, where auctions reshuffle rosters every few years. Sharma was often not a guaranteed starter, but he consistently delivered in high-pressure moments.

"Since Mumbai has a wide network of support staff, there was never a time where someone couldn't work with the players who couldn't feature in the XI. That helped me prepare and be in tune so that I can do well when opportunities come."

— Karn Sharma, on his 2017 IPL season with Mumbai Indians

His most memorable IPL contribution came during Mumbai Indians' run to their third title in 2017. After warming the bench for five weeks, Sharma was thrown into the eliminator against Kolkata Knight Riders and responded with figures of 4-16. In the final, he bowled an economical spell of 0-18 in four overs, delivering 12 dot balls.

International Career Cut Short

Sharma's international career was brief but significant. He made his T20I debut against England in September 2014, followed by his ODI debut against Sri Lanka in November that year. His Test debut came at Adelaide in December 2014, where he became the first Indian leg-spinner to debut in Australia in 25 years.

He took four wickets in the Adelaide Test, dismissing his IPL teammate David Warner twice, but conceded runs and was not selected again. India's deep spin reserves — Ravichandran Ashwin, Ravindra Jadeja, Yuzvendra Chahal and Kuldeep Yadav — left no room for a comeback at the international level.

Sharma later reflected on the experience with candor. "There's obviously a lot of regret around that game. I expected a lot better from myself but it somehow didn't happen," he told ESPNcricinfo.

A Railways Stalwart

The bulk of Sharma's career was spent with Railways in domestic cricket. Born in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, he made his first-class debut in the 2007-08 Ranji Trophy season and scored 120 on debut against Jammu and Kashmir. Over 91 first-class matches, he accumulated 2,742 runs and took 257 wickets, with a best bowling performance of 8-38.

He later moved to Vidarbha as a professional player in 2017, helping the side strengthen their spin attack under coach Chandrakant Pandit. He also represented Andhra in the 2018-19 season, where he was the leading wicket-taker in the Vijay Hazare Trophy with 12 dismissals.

A Career Beyond Headlines

Sharma went unsold at the IPL 2026 auction, effectively ending his top-level franchise career after stints with RCB in 2023-24 and a return to Mumbai Indians in 2025. His last competitive appearances came in the ongoing UP T20 League, where he played for Kanpur Superstars.

His career stats may not match those of India's frontline spinners, but his IPL record — 352 runs, consistent economy rates and that unmatched three-title run — tells the story of a player who was always ready when his team needed him most.
nri_angle: Karn Sharma's career, spent largely outside the spotlight of India's star-studded cricket system, resonates with the diaspora's appreciation for quiet persistence and the unsung contributors who make championship teams possible.
